en: The Dharma of the Great Cundī Dhāraṇī, the Heart of the Seven Buddhas and Ten Million Buddhas,
translated by Śubhakarasiṃha by Imperial Decree during the Tang Dynasty.
Namo sarvatathāgatānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ oṃ jvale jvale dhune dhune svāhā. This is the seal of the Great Maṇḍala-nī for the total subjugation of the twenty-five divisions.
With the ring fingers and little fingers of both hands interlaced within,
the two middle fingers are held upright and pressed against each other.
Bend both index fingers so they rest against the first joints of the middle fingers;
with both thumbs, pinch the middle joints of the ring fingers of the left and right hands.
If there is an invocation,
move the two index fingers back and forth.
The Buddha said that this mantra-seal can extinguish all grave offenses, including the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes.
They shall accomplish all pure dharmas;
possessing pure precepts, they will swiftly attain bodhi.
If they are householders, [they shall likewise do so].
"Even if one does not renounce alcohol, meat, or wife and children,
there is nothing that will not be accomplished provided one relies upon my Dharma.
The Buddha said, "If you seek accomplishment, first rely upon the ritual of the maṇḍala."
Unlike the extensive offerings performed by various other schools,
this [mandala] is established upon ground dug out and smeared with fragrant mud;
it uses a single-sided pure mirror that has never been used before.
On the night of the fifteenth day of the month, before an image of the Buddha,
make offerings according to one's means,
burning agalloch incense and pure water.
First, one should quiet the mind and remain free of all discursive thought;
then, forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra,
one should chant it over the mirror one hundred and eight times.
Place the mirror in a pouch or casket and always carry it with you;
later, when you wish to perform recitation, simply use this mirror.
Place it before you, form the mudrā, and recite the mantra;
by using a mirror as the altar, one will attain accomplishment.
The Buddha said that if one wishes to maintain this mantra, one should do so on the night of the fifteenth day.
Having purified oneself by bathing and donned fresh, clean garments,
one should sit in the half-lotus posture facing east,
with a mirror placed before them.
According to the availability of incense, flowers, pure water, and other such items,
one should first settle the mind and sever all discursive thoughts;
thereafter, one should form the mudrā and seal it upon the heart.
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
When reciting this mantra, it can cause short-lived sentient beings to regain increased longevity,
and even the disease of kāmalā can be cured.
How much more so for other diseases;
it is impossible that they would not be digested and cured.
The Buddha said: "If a person contemplates with single-minded tranquility..."
If one recites it twenty thousand times, forty thousand times, or sixty thousand times, there will be nothing—whether mundane or supramundane—that is not fulfilled according to one's wishes.
The Buddha said: "This applies even for laypeople."
At dawn, rinse the mouth with pure water.
Before consuming any meat or blood,
face east and, before a mirror, form the mudrā.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
If one continues in this manner for forty-nine days without interruption,
auspicious matters will arise.
The Bodhisattva Cundā causes these two holy ones to constantly follow that person, so that whatever is on their mind is explained to them one by one right by their ear.
The Buddha said: "For sentient beings who have short lifespans and many illnesses..."
On the night of the fifteenth day of the month,
burn agalloch incense and recite the mantra while forming the mudrā one hundred and eight times.
Then ghosts and demons will lose their minds, and wild foxes will be afflicted with malignant diseases.
All their own bodies will appear within the mirror;
once released, they may go as they please and shall not return again.
Their lifespan will be increased immeasurably.
The Buddha said: "If a person lacks the marks of merit and fortune,
and their petitions for office are not granted,
they should constantly recite this mantra while facing a mirror."
The officials of merit shall be able to fulfill [one's wishes].
The Buddha said: "If a person desires to accomplish anything, they should first contemplate the Noble One, Tārā."
Maintaining right mindfulness, recite this mantra seven times in full while keeping the body upright.
After a short while, the body will naturally begin to shake;
one should then know that success and auspiciousness are at hand.
If the body feels rigid and stiff when moving forward or backward, one should know that the objective will not be achieved and that calamities will surely follow.
The Buddha said: "If you wish to know whether this practice will succeed or fail," [you must observe these signs].
Having recited the mantra according to the ritual for a full seven days,
one will then see Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, flowers, and fruits in a dream;
one will spit out black matter from the mouth and subsequently consume white matter.
One will then know that accomplishment has been achieved.
The Buddha said: "This dhāraṇī possesses great power;
if you recite and uphold it with a sincere mind, you shall surely realize it for yourself."
It can cause even withered trees to bloom in flowers;
how much more so regarding the karmic rewards of the world?
If one constantly recites and maintains it, water, fire, weapons, enemies, and poisons shall all be unable to cause harm.
If someone has suddenly died from being harmed by ghosts or spirits,
one should form the mudrā and recite the mantra seven times;
by sealing the heart with the mudrā, they shall all be restored to life.
If one's residence is unstable and spirits or deities cause calamity, one should recite mantras over four clods of earth and place them as talismans; they will then depart.
The Buddha said: "If a person's six close relatives are in disharmony..."
Those who harbor no mutual affection shall,
by reciting the mantra according to the Dharma, find harmony in all they encounter;
upon hearing his name or seeing his person, they shall all give rise to joy.
Whatever one seeks will surely be fulfilled according to one's heart;
how much more so for those who can receive the complete precepts of the Upāsaka,
maintain a single-minded purity, and recite and uphold the teachings in accordance with the Dharma.
There is great power in attaining bodhi without transforming this very body.
The Buddha said: "If a person desires long life, [they should go] to ancient stupas or deep mountains."
Alternatively, within a purified chamber, one may establish a maṇḍala using a mirror as the basis.
One should complete two, four, six, or ten million recitations,
while burning blue lotuses mixed with agallochum incense.
In a dream, one dreams of eating elixirs of the immortals,
or being granted an immortal prescription, or seeing five-colored light within a mirror;
from within that light, one takes and eats the medicine at will.
One will immediately attain longevity.
The Buddha said: "If one recites and maintains this according to the Dharma with single-minded diligence, the power of its efficacy cannot be fully described."
This method of the altar-mirror must not be seen by others;
if it is seen, it will be unfavorable and the rite will not be completed.
One must keep this method secret; it cannot be explained, for one shall realize it through personal realization.
Whatever one seeks shall be swiftly accomplished, and one shall receive supreme and wondrous bliss. [End of Volume One] — Cishun.
